question: How many metric tons of net US soybean sales to China (2026/27 marketing year) will the USDA Weekly Export Sales report released September 17, 2026 show?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: weekly FAS net soybean sales to China for the current MY in early-September reporting weeks of China-engaged years (2016-22, 2024), median ~1.0 MMT; the realized 2026/27 series (0.52-1.45 MMT, median ~0.97) sits just below that. I start at ~1.0 MMT and adjust down modestly to a ~0.82 MMT median: the Sep 4-10 window holds only ~4 business days (Labor Day Sep 7 falls inside it), the one day of the window already observed produced a 250.6k flash to *unknown* rather than China, the last three published weeks trend below the early-August peak, and Sep 11 WASDE plus an expected late-September Xi visit give buyers a reason to wait. Offsetting upside: September is the seasonal peak for US-origin business (Brazil out of stock), China is only ~7.8 MMT booked against a 25 MMT pledge, a 5.54 MMT unknown book is available to switch to China as loadings begin (switches enter the net-sales column), and reporting suggests pre-summit goodwill buying. Right tail is fatter than left: a bulk switch or a multi-cargo state tranche can print >2.5 MMT (priced 5%); a negative print below -300k needs a trade rupture with no current signal (1%). No prediction market prices this, and I could not reach fas.usda.gov directly (403), so all series values are secondhand from trade press - evidence on the target week itself is genuinely near-absent, which is why I stay close to the reference class rather than reading the early-September flash pace as signal.

- Over the realized 2026/27 weekly China series (source: Brownfield Ag News, RFD-TV, UkrAgroConsult weekly write-ups): wk ending Jul 23 = 519k t; Aug 6 = 1,446k t; Aug 13 = 1,131k t; Aug 20 = 712k t; Aug 27 = 972k t. - Over early-September reporting weeks in years when China was an active buyer of US origin (2016-2022, 2024), current-MY weekly China net sales have typically fallen in the ~0.3-2.5 MMT band with median near 1.0 MMT; 2020 produced multiple weeks above 2 MMT. In 2025, with China absent on tariffs, comparable weeks were near zero.
- Over reporting weeks that contain a US federal holiday, the window has 4 rather than 5 business days.

- ADM Investor Services, Ag Market View, 2026-09-04: week ending Aug 27 China new-crop purchases of 972k t took China 2026/27 commitments to 7.761 MMT; a further 5.54 MMT stands to unknown destinations, of which the analyst estimates 50-60% is China-bound.

- ADM Investor Services, 2026-09-04: analyst puts China's effective purchases near 12 MMT and expects the halfway point of the 25 MMT pledge to be passed before Xi's Washington visit, described as ~3 weeks out (i.e. ~late September, AFTER this report).
- Economies.com / Reuters-derived, 2026-09-04: USDA confirmed 192k t to China 2026/27, following 202k t the prior day and 136k t on Tue Sep 1; total flashes to China announced since the start of September = 530k t. All three correspond to sales made Aug 31-Sep 2 (prior reporting week).
- Crisis Monitor (Greek market wire), 2026-09-07: soybean futures above $13/bu, near highest since Dec 2023; cumulative 2025/26 exports 40.76 MMT; 2026/27 outstanding sales across all destinations 16.28 MMT; 2025/26 net sales fell 94.2k t in the week ending Aug 27.
- USTR (Greer) via wire coverage, early Sep 2026: US and China expected to announce agriculture and non-tariff-barrier measures during Xi's Washington visit this month; traders watching for a cut in Chinese tariffs on US farm goods.
- The Country Today, 2026-09-06: 2026/27 US soybean sales across all destinations total 11.85 MMT, double last year's pace and the largest start in four years.
- Barchart headline, ~2026-09-04: 'Soybeans fall into the weekend as traders fade Chinese purchases' - i.e. the market treated the early-September China flashes as small relative to positioning.
- Structural: private Chinese crushers face ~13% duty on US beans vs ~3% on Brazilian origin, so nearly all current US business is state-directed (COFCO, Sinograin) and arrives in policy-timed lumps rather than on a price-driven schedule.
- Structural/seasonal: Brazilian old-crop supply is largely exhausted by September, making US origin the residual supplier for Sep-Jan; US harvest begins mid-September and vessel loadings to China ramp through October, which is when destination switches out of the Unknown book normally accelerate.
- Calendar: USDA WASDE releases 2026-09-11, one day after the window closes. USDA offices closed Mon 2026-09-07 (Labor Day). FAS reporting deadline for exporters is 11:59 pm ET the Monday after the reporting week; FAS publishes Thursdays 08:30 ET.
- Counter-direction: analysts through mid-2026 remained skeptical the 25 MMT/yr pledge would be met; USDA balance sheets assume closer to 15 MMT of Chinese buying for 2026/27.

STATUS QUO OUTCOME: absent a policy event, the report prints another week in the same band the 2026/27 series has occupied since July - a mid-to-high six-figure to low-seven-figure positive number, driven by state-directed cargo tranches plus any destination reassignments, with no mechanism currently pushing it negative.

SEARCHED FOR BUT COULD NOT FIND: (a) any prediction market or bookmaker pricing this quantity - Polymarket and Manifold title searches returned nothing and no Kalshi contract on FAS weekly export sales surfaced; (b) the published week-ending-Sep-3 figure (not released until 2026-09-10); (c) any USDA daily flash announcement dated Sep 8 or later (none exist yet as of Now); (d) direct fas.usda.gov pages - the site returned HTTP 403 to every fetch attempt, so all series values here are secondhand from trade press; (e) a published trade-estimate range specifically for China's share of the Sep-10-week sales (only all-destination soybean ranges of 12-65 and 45-95 mil bu were quoted, and those attach to earlier reports); (f) a confirmed date for the Xi Washington visit.
calls.reference_class: Weekly USDA FAS net export sales of U.S. soybeans to China for the then-current marketing year, in the first-half-of-September reporting weeks of years when China was an active buyer of U.S. origin (2016-2022, 2024), combined with the realized 2026/27 weekly China series from July-August 2026

calls.reasoning: Reference class is the 2026/27 China weekly new-crop net-sales series under the state-directed buying program: median ~1.05 MMT, last four weeks 1,446/1,131/1,102/972 kt. I shade the median below that because (a) the four-week trend is a clean ~13%/week decay, (b) the window contains Labor Day, giving 4 business days not 5, (c) prices sit above $13/bu near 26-month highs, which historically stalls Chinese state buying, and (d) buyers may wait for the Sept 11 WASDE, one day after the window closes, and hold announcements for the Sept 24 Xi White House visit. Offsetting upside: the 2026/27 MY began Sept 1, so unknown-destination balances (669 kt added the week of Aug 27, 250.6 kt on Sept 3) begin switching to China as positive net sales, and China needs roughly 1 MMT/week to stay near the 25 MMT pledge. Crucially I observe nothing inside the target window - the widely-cited ~530 kt of early-September flashes were sales made Aug 31-Sep 2 and land in the prior reporting week - so dispersion stays near full reference-class width rather than being narrowed by within-window data. Upper escape priced for a pre-summit block purchase plus large unknown-to-China reassignment; lower escape requires net washouts beyond 300 kt, which nothing in the evidence supports.

TIMING MECHANICS (load-bearing): a sale is counted in the reporting week in which the CONTRACT was made, not the week it was announced. USDA daily-sale announcements (required for >=100,000 t of one commodity to one destination in one day) are published the next business day. Therefore sales contracted Sept 4 are announced Tue Sept 8 (Mon Sept 7 is the holiday), and sales contracted Thu Sept 10 are announced Fri Sept 11 - after the window closes but before the Sept 17 release. No daily announcement covering any part of this window had been published as of Now.

calls.reasoning: Reference class: the six published weeks of 2026/27 China net soybean sales (Jul 9-Aug 27 2026), mean ~1.04 MMT, SD ~0.30 MMT, range 0.52-1.45 MMT. Status quo for a one-week-ahead print is continuation near 1 MMT. I shade the median slightly below the class mean to ~0.95 MMT: the window has only 4 business days (Labor Day Sept 7), the last four weeks trend down (1.446 -> 1.131 -> 1.101 -> 0.972), beans above $13 are the highest since Dec 2023, and 16.28 MMT of new-crop is already booked (36% of USDA's projection), so state buyers may hold deliverables for the Sept 24 Xi visit rather than book them in this window. Offsetting and holding the right tail fat: September is seasonally the heaviest booking month, pre-summit accumulation is documented, and switches out of a multi-MMT 'unknown' book now post as China net sales. Crucially, none of the widely-quoted 530k of early-September flashes fall in this window - they were transacted Aug 31-Sept 2 and belong to the week ending Sept 3 - and the only Sept 4 flash was 250,600 t to unknown, so I have no direct read on the target week and stay close to the base rate with wide bars. p_above_upper 0.025 prices a pre-summit mega-tender exceeding 2.5 MMT (no week in this regime has exceeded 1.45 MMT); p_below_lower 0.01 prices a trade rupture forcing >300k of net COFCO/Sinograin washouts inside one week. No human market prices this contract, so no blend.

- Private Chinese crushers still face a ~13% duty on U.S. beans vs ~3% on Brazilian origin, so essentially all current buying is state-directed (COFCO, Sinograin). Any tariff cut would enlarge the buyer pool but would land after the window.
- Sinograin was scheduled to auction another 68,000 t of previously purchased beans on Sept 9, 2026 (reserve-release activity, which runs opposite to fresh import demand).
- 2026/27 total outstanding sales, all destinations: 16.28 MMT as of the w/e Aug 27 release. Cumulative 2026/27 exports/commitments context: 2025/26 cumulative exports 40.76 MMT with 1.10 MMT outstanding.
- Price/crop: November beans near 26-month highs above $13/bu; USDA national soybean condition rating at a multi-year low with hot, dry late-season weather; a WASDE lands Sept 11, 2026 (inside the window's tail, after most transaction days).
- Mechanism note for the China line specifically: as the U.S. shipping season opens, cargoes previously booked to 'Unknown' get switched, and a switch to China posts as a POSITIVE net sale on the China line in the same weekly report. The unknown book has been large (669,000 t added w/e Aug 27; 250,600 t on Sept 4).
- Opposite mechanism: net sales are net of cancellations and of switches OUT of China; Chinese washouts of prior purchases have occurred in prior trade-friction episodes.
- Sentiment marker: a Sept 5, 2026 grains wrap attributed session weakness to 'weaker Chinese buying' and framed the coming sessions as a test of whether that is a pause or a shift.

calls.reasoning: Resolves off one cell: soybeans / China PRC / 2026-2027 net sales in the Sep 17 FAS release, covering Fri Sep 4 - Thu Sep 10. Reconciled fact that moves the number: NO flash announcement observed so far falls inside that window. The 530k of Sep 1-3 China flashes and the Sep 4 250.6k unknown-destination flash are all Aug 31 - Sep 3 transactions belonging to the Sep 10 release; two runs mistakenly read the Sep 4 announcement as within-window bearish evidence. So this is a near-pure base-rate call. The 2026/27 series has printed 200/519/904/972/1056/1102/1131/1446 kt (median ~1.01 MMT). I shade to 880k for four business days (Labor Day Sep 7), the softening late-August cadence, and beans above $13 near 26-month highs (state buyers historically step in on dips); I do not shade further because the Sep 1-3 flash clip times the observed 1.5-2x flash-to-net multiplier implies ~1.0 MMT, and Unknown-to-China destination switches now post as positive China net sales with the MY current from Sep 1. Right tail stays fat: a pre-summit state block or a switch wave can double the print. Negative prints need net washouts, for which nothing in the evidence argues.
calls.reconciliation: The load-bearing correction was factual, not a weighing: two runs treated the Sep 4 flash announcement as an in-window observation, when the one-business-day announcement lag places that transaction on Sep 3, in the prior reporting week. Once that is removed, NO run holds any information about Sep 4-10, so the estimate must be the reference-class distribution for one more week of the state-directed program adjusted for a four-day week - not a reading of a soft early-September flash pace. I carried forward Run 3's reference class (the published 2026/27 China weekly prints) because all four converged on the same series and the same median near 1.0 MMT. I did not carry any run's dispersion: Run 2's 1.0 MMT is internally inconsistent with its own no-within-window-read finding, and Run 4's 1.55 MMT over-widens against six consecutive prints in a 0.9-1.45 MMT band; I recomputed from realized SD (~0.35 MMT) inflated for the observation gap and regime novelty. The 7.76 vs 12 MMT dispute over China's cumulative book could not be settled - fas.usda.gov was 403 to every run and no primary table was ever read, so every series value in every dossier is secondhand trade press, which is itself a reason to keep the bars wide. Median 880k sits just below the runs' 820-950k span midpoint by construction rather than by averaging: the holiday and price-level drags are real, but the flash-multiplier arithmetic (~710k flash-only x 1.5-2x) and live switch-eligibility keep it from falling into the low 800s. No web access on this run; sources is empty and correct.
